model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026 net operating income (after credit and other impairment charges), consolidated income statement MQG.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:11143
inputs.share_count_basis: FY2026 weighted average ordinary shares net of treasury shares adjusted for vested MEREP awards (367,412,547) PLUS unvested MEREP awards (9,457,781) from the diluted-EPS reconciliation, MQG.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:11854-11858. The 14,725,080 potential shares from the dilutive convertible subordinated notes (BCN3/MCN5/MCN7) are EXCLUDED because their $A168m interest is already charged inside attributable NPAT; including both would double-charge (difference ~0.4%/share). Count held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction: Macquarie is an APRA-regulated bank holding company and its issued debt securities, borrowings and loan capital ($A167,944m at 31-Mar-26, per core_metrics) and deposits ($A221,547m, kpis) are operating funding whose cost is already inside net operating income. Cash and liquid assets ($A23,422m) are held against that funding. The flow capitalised is FCFE (attributable NPAT less capital retained to fund growth) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026 FCFE proxy = ordinary dividends declared for FY2026 ($A7.00/share x 379.6m = $A2,657m; no on-market buyback in FY2026). Equals attributable NPAT $A4,847m less $A2,190m retained to fund the year's 13% income growth. reported_fcf is the same figure before the MEREP charge (2,657 + 837) so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.sbc_source: MQG.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:17890 cash-flow reconciliation 'Share-based payments expense' 837 (FY2025: 843). MEREP awards are settled from treasury shares bought on-market ($A881m in FY2026, kpis TreasurySharesPurchased), so there is no separate net-share-settlement tax line to add.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income ($A18,798m gross, $A4,151m net) IS the banking business, not a return on surplus cash, and no cash is added to the valuation.
inputs.buyback_note: On-market buyback concluded: $A644m FY2024, $A369m FY2025, nil FY2026. Management has said no further purchases are currently expected; capital is being redeployed into growth. The flat count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge, not by repurchases.
inputs.book_value_anchor: Ordinary shareholders' equity $A36,068m (ex-NCI $A788m); intangibles $A2,211m -> tangible book $A33,857m ($A89.83/share on 376.9m). FY2026 ROE 14.0% reported (13.4% on year-end equity); 11-year average ROE ~15% (FY24-25 trough 10.5-11.2%, FY22-23 peak 16.5-18.7%). Group capital surplus $A9.3bn; Bank Group CET1 12.8% APRA / 17.5% harmonised.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in AUD, the currency of the flows: AUD 10-year Commonwealth bond ~4.3% (Sept 2026) + beta 1.15 x Australian equity risk premium 5.4% = 10.5%. Beta above the domestic big-four banks (~1.0) for the markets-facing CGM trading and Macquarie Capital principal-investing income. One rate across all three scenarios; regulatory (APRA overlay, Shield/ASIC) and cyclical risk is charged in the bear flows and in the 25% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial ($A804m liabilities vs $A36bn equity); lease cost sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. NCI profit share is $A22m (0.45% of PAT) and is absorbed in the 27.5% cash-tax-rate driver (27.6% effective tax + ~0.3% NCI leakage). No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (as IAG.AX, GMG.AX, CHC.AX). Macquarie is an APRA-regulated NOHC of an ADI; the financial-parser deliberately left free cash flow empty because OCF is dominated by deposit/loan/trading movements (FY2023 -11.4bn, FY2022 +50.5bn), so the owner-FCF DCF would be meaningless. Engine mapping: revenue = net operating income; ebitda_margin_path = profit before tax + MEREP expense as % of income (FY2026 38.85%; FY22-26 range 33.3-41.3%, mean 37.7%); sbc_pct_path = MEREP expense (4.3%); da_pct = 0; capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund growth, = NPAT margin x g/ROE (the clean-surplus identity FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROE)); cash_tax_rate_path = 27.5%; wacc = cost of equity; net_debt = 0. FY0 reconciliation: 19,477 x (38.85% - 4.3%) x (1 - 27.5%) = 4,879 vs reported attributable NPAT 4,847. Residual-income cross-check on book: P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) = (14.5 - 3)/(10.5 - 3) = 1.53x x $A36,068m = ~$A147/share, which the engine base should approximate. The $A9.3bn regulatory capital surplus is NOT added as a bridge item: the earnings it produces are already in NPAT and a book-based method values it through ROE. FY2026 one-offs (OnStream meter divestment, sale of North American/European public investments, equity exits) are why the FY27 base margin steps down from 38.85% to 36.5% and FY27 income growth is only 4%. Price is the ASX regular close, not volatile. H1 FY2027 (Sept-26 half) is not yet reported (due early Nov 2026); FY2026 is the latest balance sheet.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is attributable NPAT, which is already after the MEREP (SBC) expense; the 'FCF' CAGRs are NPAT CAGRs. SBC grew 10.9%/yr over 10 years vs NPAT 8.9%: a slowly rising share of income is paid in stock (3.0% of income FY2016 -> 4.3% FY2026).
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average net operating income growth (4% FY27 stepping to 7% then tapering to 3.5%), anchored between the 10-year revenue CAGR (6.7%) and the FY26 one-off-inflated base; below the 10-year NPAT CAGR (8.9%) and equity CAGR (9.1%).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-year CAGRs (revenue 0.6%, EPS -1.3%, equity 2.8%) are all measured from the FY2023 commodity-volatility peak (NPAT 5,182, ROE 16.9%) and understate trend; 5- and 10-year CAGRs agree within 2pp (8.8-10.3% / 6.7-9.1%). No >30% divergence on the longer windows.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC profit-before-tax margin on net operating income. FY26 38.85% includes divestment gains; FY27 steps to 36.5% as they roll off, then 37.0% = FY22-26 mean (37.7%) less a little for BFS margin competition and rising impairments.
base.capex_note: Capital retained to fund growth = NPAT margin (~23.7% of income) x g / ROE, with sustainable ROE 14.5% (11-year average ~15%, FY26 14.0%). At 7% growth 48% of NPAT is retained (payout 52%); at 3.5% growth 24% (payout 76%, i.e. the 70% policy ceiling plus buybacks). Terminal 3% growth would need 5.0%; the 5.7% carried into the terminal year is a small conservatism.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-SBC PBT margin toward the FY22-23 level (40.5-41.3%) as CGM volatility income, MAM performance fees and Macquarie Capital exits stay elevated.
bull.capex_note: Retention = NPAT margin (~25.2%) x g / ROE at sustainable ROE 16% (FY22-23 delivered 16.5-18.7%).

bear.ebitda_margin_note: FY27 at 32.0% carries Shield-related class-action/remediation costs and higher impairments on top of the one-off roll-off; thereafter the FY24-25 trough level (33.3-34.4%).
bear.capex_note: Retention = NPAT margin (~21.2%) x g / ROE at ROE 11.5% (FY24-25 delivered 10.5-11.2%). Lower ROE means more capital per unit of growth, which is the bank-model penalty for regulatory capital overlays.

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 income grows 4% as the FY26 divestment gains (OnStream, public-investments sale, equity exits) roll off against underlying growth in all four franchises; the pre-SBC pre-tax margin steps from 38.9% to 36.5% so NPAT is roughly flat, then income compounds 7% for two years on MAM's infrastructure/private-credit AUM (Qube, MIP VI, data-centre and energy-transition platforms), BFS share gains and CGM's energy-transition footprint, tapering to 3.5% by FY36. Sustainable ROE 14.5% (11-year average ~15%) sets how much of NPAT must be retained to fund that growth, so the distributable share of earnings rises from ~52% to ~76% as growth slows. APRA overlays are worked off on schedule and no further material conduct charges arise.
scenario_narratives.bull: CGM's commodity/energy volatility income and financing book keep compounding (CGM +49% in FY26 becomes a new base rather than a peak), MAM performance fees and Macquarie Capital realisations stay elevated, and the pre-tax margin returns toward the FY22-23 level (40-41%). Income grows 8-9% for three years and ROE holds 16%, so growth is funded with less retained capital and payout plus buybacks can rise. Terminal growth 3.5%. Even here the value is bounded by the 10.5% cost of equity: at ROE 16% the justified P/B is ~1.8x, not the 2.5x the market pays.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY27 income is flat as the one-offs unwind and a weaker deal/volatility backdrop hits CGM and Macquarie Capital; the margin drops to 32% with Shield Master Fund class-action and remediation costs plus impairment charges continuing to rise (already +96% in FY26); the $A500m APRA operational-risk overlay and liquidity add-ons persist, holding ROE at the FY24-25 level (11.5%) so every unit of growth consumes more capital. Growth recovers only to 3-4% and terminal growth is 2.5%. AUD strength on >80% offshore income in MAM/CGM/MacCap is a further translation drag not separately modelled.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 25%: an open regulatory dependency on a single regulator (APRA capital and liquidity overlays only partially eased, Shield Master Fund proceedings and possible class actions, an ASIC settlement in March 2026, a remuneration strike) and the FY26 result leaning on one-off gains. Bull cut to 25%: it needs CGM volatility income, MAM performance fees AND Macquarie Capital exits to all stay at cycle-high levels simultaneously, and ROE has not held above 16% for more than two consecutive years.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Macquarie is valued as what it is: an APRA-regulated bank holding company whose distributable earnings are NPAT less the capital it must retain to grow. Those flows are capitalised at a 10.5% AUD cost of equity with net debt at zero, which is equivalent to residual income on book. The engine build and the residual-income shortcut (P/B = (ROE - g)/(CoE - g)) both put fair value near 1.5x book, against a market price of ~2.5x book and ~19x FY26 EPS. The gap is not a forecasting disagreement about FY27 -- it is the market discounting Macquarie's flows at roughly 7.5-8% or assuming its 13-15% ROE compounds at high-single-digit growth indefinitely. Both scenarios are shown in the required-return table so the reader can see what return today's price implies rather than take the base case on faith.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: every 1pp on the 10.5% rate moves value roughly 15-20%; at 9% the base case is materially higher. The rate is the single largest judgment in the model.
Sustainable ROE: the model retains NPAT x g/ROE; if incremental ROE is closer to the FY22-23 16-19% than the 14.5% base, less capital is consumed and value rises toward the bull case.
FY26 one-off gains: if the OnStream / public-investments / equity-exit gains are larger than the ~2.4pp margin step-down assumed, FY27 NPAT falls more than the flat base implies.

Regulatory: APRA $A500m operational-risk overlay unchanged, liquidity add-on only cut 25%->15%; Shield Master Fund proceedings and possible class actions can add conduct costs beyond the $A321m already paid.
Earnings mix: CGM (42% of FY26 net profit contribution) and Macquarie Capital (15%) are volatility- and deal-cycle dependent; a two-year down cycle looks like the FY24-25 trough (ROE 10.5-11%).
Currency: >80% of MAM, CGM and Macquarie Capital income is earned offshore; FY26 equity fell $A1.7bn on FX translation. AUD appreciation reduces AUD earnings independently of the franchise.
Terminal assumption: ~55% of base value sits in the terminal (Gordon at 3% binds below the 15x FCFE cap); each 0.5pp of terminal growth is ~7% of value.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (ASX regular close); 52-week range 187.31-267.905.
data_sources.financials: MQG.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, AUD millions, FY2015-FY2026 annual + H1 FY2016-H1 FY2026 halves) exported from MQG.AX.duckdb; kpis table for Deposits, NetInterestIncome, NetLoans, DividendsPaid, TreasurySharesPurchased, ShareRepurchases; FY2026 Annual Report (MQG.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt) for the income statement (line 11143-11157), diluted-EPS reconciliation (11840-11860), capital position (1936-1965), intangibles (13271-13279) and five-year summary (9713-9719).
data_sources.qualitative: MQG.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-24): segment mix, growth drivers, regulatory developments (APRA overlays Feb 2026, ASIC settlement Mar 2026, Shield Master Fund), Qube Holdings acquisition (completed Aug 2026), bull/bear cases.
